top_news.title: New York Seizes a Dozen Celebrity Deepfake Websites
top_news.dek: The Manhattan District Attorney’s Office has seized 12 websites linked to the creation and distribution of non-consensual celebrity deepfakes.
top_news.brief: The legal action targets sites that collectively impacted approximately 1,200 victims. This represents a significant enforcement effort against platforms facilitating the generation of harmful AI-synthesized content.
top_news.image_alt: Gavel resting on a digital screen showing abstract data patterns

top_news.title: Fundamental Dynamical Units for Physics-Informed Structural Inference from Perturbation Time-Series in Networked Systems
top_news.dek: Researchers propose a new framework for inferring signed interaction structures in networked dynamical systems from perturbation time-series data.
top_news.brief: The study addresses the challenge of recovering interaction structures in complex networked systems. By tackling combinatorial complexity, causal ambiguity, and state-dependent dynamics, the authors introduce a physics-informed approach to structural inference, aiming to improve mechanistic understanding of networked dynamical systems.
top_news.image_alt: Diagram showing networked nodes and perturbation flow

top_news.title: Data Loss Prevention - Discover where sensitive data goes before you create a Data Loss Prevention policy
top_news.dek: Cloudflare has introduced Passive Detection for its Data Loss Prevention (DLP) service to help teams map sensitive data flows before enforcing policies.
top_news.brief: The feature analyzes sampled HTTP traffic to identify sensitive data types and destinations without requiring active blocking rules. This allows administrators to gain visibility into organizational data movement and refine DLP policies based on actual traffic patterns.
top_news.image_alt: Dashboard interface showing data flow analytics and traffic patterns

top_news.title: Notes on gotchas while migrating 35kb preprompts from Opus to self-hosted Ollama
top_news.dek: Migrating large system prompts to local Ollama instances reveals significant differences in model behavior and performance compared to proprietary APIs.
top_news.brief: A developer details the challenges of moving 35kb system prompts from Claude to self-hosted Ollama. The transition highlights how local models handle complex instructions differently, emphasizing the importance of session metadata and the risks of relying on third-party providers for sensitive problem-solving transcripts.
top_news.image_alt: Diagram showing prompt migration flow from cloud APIs to local Ollama infrastructure

top_news.title: Reward AI Releases OM-1: A Robot Policy Trained on Human Demonstrations Only, With No Teleoperation or On-Robot Data
top_news.dek: Reward AI's OM-1 is a general-purpose robot policy trained exclusively on human demonstrations using wearable glove tracking.
top_news.brief: OM-1 achieves manipulation tasks on industrial arms and humanoids without teleoperation or on-robot training data. By utilizing electromagnetic hand tracking, the model reduces overshoot by 60% compared to visual-inertial methods and can learn new tasks from under 30 minutes of human demonstration data.
top_news.image_alt: Robotic arm performing manipulation tasks using OM-1 policy

primary.title: Sakana AI Researchers Introduce PC-ALM, a Layer-Local Alternative to Backpropagation That Trains 1000-Layer Networks
primary.summary: Sakana AI researchers Jeffrey Seely and Julian Gould introduce Augmented Lagrangian Predictive Coding (PC-ALM), a local-learning alternative to backpropagation. By attaching a Lagrange multiplier to each layer constraint, PC-ALM keeps predictive coding's layer-local updates while recovering exact backprop gradients in linear networks. It matches BP across widths and depths from 8 to 128 at an inference budget of T = 2L, lifts gradient cosine to BP from 0.604 to 0.909 in the reference cell, and trains 1000-layer residual MLPs within about 2 points of backprop on MNIST.
